title: He Mows With His Eyes SHUT
premise: Our neighbor Mr. Odell has the greenest lawn on the street and his mower only runs at 3 AM. Everyone on our street obeys one rule: never look at his lawn while the mower is running. My dad has lost a lawn war to him for ten years, because ours has one perfectly round bald spot, and he sets an alarm to catch him cheating.
twist: The street is built on a giant sleeping head. Mr. Odell's lawn is its eyebrow, our bald spot is where its hairline is going, and when he trims the brow the eye under the turf wakes and turns toward whoever is watching, tipping every house on it. Mr. Odell mows with his eyes shut so it never turns to him. Dad shuts his, the street settles, and the two rivals become a crew of two.
world: a bright suburban cul-de-sac at three in the morning: a floodlit stripe-mown lawn with a low oval hump, a butter yellow house with a blinded upstairs window, a leaning coral house across the street, a low white fence, plain mailboxes and a red push mower on an orange cord
